title: Why do we reach for our phones the moment we're bored?

voice.style: calm, intimate, close-mic narrator speaking directly to one person; thoughtful and unhurried but not slow, like a premium short documentary; crisp diction, low energy, no hype

music.prompt: Instrumental only, absolutely no vocals, no choir. A dark, intimate, minimal underscore for a short film about the mind, about 90 seconds. Mood: hushed, introspective, slightly uneasy, quietly beautiful. Slow pulse around 68 BPM. Instrumentation: deep soft sub bass, warm detuned analog synth pad, sparse felt piano single notes with long reverb, a faint ticking clock-like percussion texture, subtle tape hiss. Very spacious, lots of silence between notes. Structure: starts almost empty, slowly thickens, a gentle lift two thirds in, then thins out and ends cleanly on a held low note. Mixed to sit under a quiet voiceover: no sudden hits, no melody hooks, no drums.
